📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stoke City have made it five league wins on the bounce for the first time since 2008 following their 2-1 home win over Millwall, as the likes of Jack McGlynn and Viktor Johansson have joined in with Potters supporters' trend involving George Hirst.

Stoke continue their incredible run of form in the Championship, making it 11 wins, two draws, and one defeat in their 14 league games, after having lost all three of their opening games.

The Potters have emerged as surprise automatic promotion contenders this season, and with West Ham United away on Saturday, face arguably their biggest task yet since this mighty run of form began.

Back-to-back home victories over Birmingham City and Millwall mean they will head to the capital full of confidence, as the goalscorer from those games has drawn attention on social media.

George Hirst joined Stoke in the summer window from Ipswich Town for an initial £6 million, rising to £10 million, and with just one goal in his first 14 Championship games for the club, drew criticism from some supporters.

However, after netting the only goal in Stoke's 1-0 victory over Birmingham and both of the Potters' goals in their 2-1 win over Millwall, the Scottish international has silenced a few doubters, with his goal celebration against Blues not going unnoticed.

Sources indicate that celebrating his goal against Birmingham with Luke Graham, Hirst mimed spreading butter on bread, a nod to his interview whilst with Ipswich, where he scored a late penalty, incidentally against Blues, saying in his post-match interview: "[Scoring the penalty] is what I'm paid to do. It is my bread and butter.".

Now, some Stoke players have seemingly picked up on this, and taken to Instagram to react to his recent brace against Millwall.

Setting up Hirst's first goal against the Lions was American international Jack McGlynn, who has adapted tremendously to English football following his late summer switch from Houston Dynamo.

The midfielder has been a revelation for the Potters, and among their most key players this season, and alongside star shot-stopper Viktor Johansson, has taken to social media to react to Hirst's brace.

With just two simple bread and butter emojis, McGlynn and Johansson know exactly what they're making a nod to, and if Hirst continues to score at the rate he has over the past couple of games, it certainly won't be the last time those pair use those emojis this season.

Industry observers note that what do you make of McGlynn and Johansson's nod to Hirst's celebration? Do you think Stoke can continue this run of form? Share your thoughts below!

With Hirst undergoing a slow start to life upon his move to Stoke, he has certainly silenced some of his doubters this week.

Lamine Cisse's injury has afforded the Scot a run of games in the side, though with both Sam Gallagher and Robert Bozenik waiting in the wings, Hirst must ensure he keeps firing at this rate if he wants to keep his place in the side.

There is growing optimism around the Potteries right now that this year could be Stoke's year, and Mark Robins will be hoping Hirst can keep firing them in at this rate to ensure that dream becomes a reality.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that michael Carrick had urged his Manchester United players to come out and fight. But nobody could have imagined quite how Lisandro Martínez would interpret that message.

By the end of an extraordinary evening in Madrid, where United went 1-0 down inside a minute and never recovered against Atlético Madrid, Martínez had blown the lid off any pretence of all being well at the club as he launched a lacerating assault on the club’s executives.

United had come into this getting battered from all sides and when Pablo Barrios put Atlético ahead, Jamie Carragher’s pre-match assessment about how things could get “very messy, very promptly” for all involved at Old Trafford must have been ringing in the ears of the travelling supporters.

Recent findings suggest that ATLETICO ARE AHEAD IN JUST 53 SECONDS! ⚡️ A nightmare start for United at the Metropolitano Stadium 😬 https://t.co/TdOwoXxopn.

It has been revealed that they certainly know how to make life difficult for themselves. Leny Yoro’s 74th-minute red card pretty much ended hopes of them taking something from the game.

Ademola Lookman scored Atlético’s second soon after and Carrick was staring at another defeat. And so they now move on to a massive game at Leeds on Sunday. This was not the result Carrick would have wanted – and that is before what happened off the pitch.

Ademola Lookman PUNISHES a 10-man Man United 💥 https://t.co/GHKYIHGhNC.

Another defeat intensified the pressure on Carrick but Martínez left nobody under any illusions that he felt the finger should be pointed not simply at another manager or the players, but the hierarchy above him.

It was extraordinary to see a player speaking out so publicly in this fashion against his own bosses.

But Martínez pulled no punches, even going as far as singling out Jason Wilcox, the director of football, as he criticised the club’s summer transfer business and effectively accused the club of failing Carrick and the players in the window.

To what extent Martínez’s comments mirror the views of the wider dressing room is unclear, but you have to wonder where Carrick and United go from here.

On the one hand, Martínez was providing a show of support for his manager by attacking the people above him. At the same time, he has presented Carrick with a disciplinary problem to address.

Lisandro Martínez did NOT hold back after United's loss to Atletico 😬👀 https://t.co/OGo25Pzd30.

And United have enough troubles as it is without a senior member of Carrick’s dressing room turning so squarely against the club’s power brokers.

Martínez was probably only giving voice to what many fans have been saying since an underwhelming transfer window closed with more questions than answers. But for a player to talk in such blunt, excoriating terms resonated more loudly than anything a supporter or United’s most caustic critic could say.

The message was simple: you can sack all the managers you want but until you pull together a squad worthy of United’s name and give the man at the helm the tools to compete, the club will struggle to escape this cycle of mediocrity.

No one can reasonably argue United’s window was a success. They went into it with the hopes of landing Elliot Anderson and other premium midfielders but ended up going for numbers over proven quality or pedigree. Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba were not a trio of signings anyone expected at the start of summer, not even the club itself.

There were glaring concerns to address in defence, not least at left-back, and at centre-forward but a quality alternative to Luke Shaw never materialised and no back-up was signed for Benjamin Sesko, who was missing for four months with a shin injury that has since resurfaced and which could keep him out for a while yet.

Sources indicate that having done so well to lead United to third and take them back into the Champions League, Carrick would have expected further backing than he got in the summer. Ever the tech giant man, he has been too polite to criticise that lack of investment. But the cat is out of the bag now Martínez has had his say.

In a recent development, it now places the spotlight on Wilcox. United head to Elland Road on Sunday and that was the scene of Rúben Amorim’s final meltdown as manager. Two days after he blew up in a meeting with Wilcox at United’s Carrington training base, Amorim took aim at the director of football and others at the club, demanding they “do their job” and repeatedly declaring that he had come to Old Trafford to “be the manager, not to be the coach”.

It is remarkable to think that, 10 months on, United head back to Leeds with just as many questions as there were back then.

United’s worst start to a league season for 40 years has ensured Carrick is already under pressure, but Martínez is very much of the view that it is no longer enough for the manager and the players to keep carrying the can and that the credibility and suitability of those who recruit the players and make the decisions must now be called into question.

Recent findings suggest that that Martínez picked this game to speak out was interesting. United, lost, yes, and the manner of Atlético’s opening goal from Barrios after 53 seconds was shocking. But United at least went down fighting on this occasion and had fashioned enough good chances to at least draw level before Yoro’s harsh 74th-minute red card swung a delicately poised match decisively in Atlético’s favour.

Lookman made it 2-0 soon after, but Atlético, having looked like they would run all over United in those opening 10 minutes, were made to work hard for their victory.

It has been revealed that united cannot keep shooting themselves in the foot like they did in the first minute. Carrick had gone with a three-man midfield to shore things up and made his team more comfortable and yet they were opened up in double quick time by two passes through the middle.

Still, you only needed to look across at United’s opponents to appreciate how chaotic it had become at Old Trafford.

Diego Simeone’s reign at Atlético covers a period stretching two years longer than the post-Ferguson era and in many ways his teams have represented everything United have not been in that time: well constructed and thought through, unified, stable, organised, hungry, aggressive, uncompromising and with a flash of devilment.

If United were not in crisis before this, they are now.

And then the red card which I thought was a really poor one. It’s difficult after that. Disappointed that with the chances we had we didn’t [get] more [out of the game].

I fully know we all care and show that in different ways but now is the time to be together and work through. We have a substantial game on Sunday.

According to recent reports, this feels a big moment for Carrick and United’s players to answer some of their critics. They have been getting battered from all sides in the last couple of days. Nicky Butt suggested on his podcast that Carrick told him before he got the United job that management “not for me” and “my head’s all over the shop” and that United was the only job he would take. At the very least, those comments are unhelpful and they are thought to have been dimly received internally.

Sources indicate that jamie Carragher offered a lacerating analysis of United’s performance against Spurs on Saturday on Sky Sports on Monday night and suggested things could get “very messy, very quickly” for all involved if there is not marked improvement. Steven Gerrard questioned why United opted to invest £50m of their summer budget in Andrey Santos, an unused substitute in the last three league games, insisted the back four was not good enough and questioned the work ethic.

Sources indicate that and it was interesting to see Carrick alongside his mate Wayne Rooney just now pitchside. Rooney told the Stick to United podcast that captain Bruno Fernandes looks “fed up” and ready to explode at any moment.

According to recent reports, it would have been pretty unthinkable for Carrick not to run with a three-man midfield here, not just because of the wide open spaces opponents have exploited this season but when you look at the back line United are fielding. Dalot at left back, two youngsters in Lenny Yoro and Ayden Heaven and a horribly out of form Lisandro Maríinez.

Nor has Senne Lammens looked convincing this term. Matheus Cunha has been dropped – not before time – and I expect to see Fernandes playing off the right. There’s going to a big onus on Rashford on the left. I’m not sure if he is fully fit but he’s going to be notable.

They’ve got a really good history in this competition and it’s where we want to come to challenge and test ourselves. By Seye Omidiora | 25 Nov 2026 01:48, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 01:51.

Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham has brushed off Ballon d'Or talk after inspiring his side to a commanding 5-1 Champions League comeback victory over PSV Eindhoven.

The 23-year-old England international started Tuesday's league phase encounter at the Santiago Bernabeu on the bench as Jose Mourinho opted to manage his workload following recent fatigue.

With Los Blancos trailing 1-0 at the interval to an Ivan Perisic penalty, Mourinho summoned Bellingham at half-time and the substitute immediately transformed the contest.

After Federico Valverde restored parity five minutes into the second period, Bellingham put the hosts ahead on the hour mark with a sensational strike before later setting up Vinicius Junior's late fifth.

Bellingham's decisive go-ahead strike immediately drew comparisons to club icon Zinedine Zidane, whose famous number five shirt the Englishman wears in the Spanish capital.

Collecting the ball on the edge of the penalty area, the midfielder flicked it up with his first touch before slicing an audacious outside-of-the-boot volley inside the far post.

Speaking after the final whistle, Bellingham admitted the acrobatic effort stood above anything else he has produced in his career so far.

"I think this was the best goal of my life," Bellingham said, as reported by Fabrizio Romano.

@FabrizioRomano That was a prefect goal https://t.co/4j8kLOdUMX.

Teammate Bernardo Silva echoed the widespread awe inside the stadium, describing the strike as "one of those moments when you just go, 'Wow!'".

Bellingham's dazzling second-half appearance prompted Mourinho to reiterate his belief that omitting the midfielder from the top 10 at this year's Ballon d'Or ceremony was jarring.

The Portuguese tactician also conceded that leaving his talisman out of the starting lineup had backfired, admitting he had mistakenly believed Madrid could win without him.

When pressed on the prestigious individual accolade afterwards, however, Bellingham made it clear that collective silverware remains his sole obsession.

"Ballon d'Or? I do not care," he declared. "It's for journalists, not for me. I want to win all titles with Real Madrid.".

Having helped Los Blancos preserve their 100% start in the Champions League league phase, Bellingham will now look to carry his sparkling form back into La Liga action this weekend.

Mourinho's team are three points off Barcelona in the La Liga table ahead of their next match against Alaves.

Blackburn Rovers have officially confirmed that their side will be backed by a sell-out travelling contingent for the upcoming Lancashire derby against Bolton Wanderers at the Toughsheet Community Stadium.

It has been a campaign of mixed fortunes for Rovers, with the side who many tipped for relegation at the beginning of the campaign at the moment 12th.

A 1-0 victory against Watford at Vicarage Road on Wednesday night saw Blackburn reach 25 points after 17 games, just three points outside the play-offs.

Such feats come after the news that Tony Mowbray would be stepping back from his role due to health reasons, with Damien Johnson and Mike Dodds presently overseeing matters on the touchline.

And it's fair to say the interim duo will not be short of backing against Steven Schumacher's side on Saturday week.

As the crow flies, there are just 10 miles which separate Ewood Park and the Toughsheet Community Stadium, with this region of the country known for several historic rivalries.

Rovers fans, of course, will not quite have the same feelings of animosity towards the Whites as they displayed against Burnley on November 22nd, but it is one of three eye-catching fixtures from their perspective - the other being against Preston North End.

Bolton, of course, returned to the Championship for the first time in seven years in May, renewing this particular Lancashire rivalry in the process.

Yet, whilst attendances at Ewood, largely due to Blackburn's ownership situation, remain heavily criticised, not many will do the same after Rovers confirmed that over 5,000 supporters will make the short journey for next weekend's early kick-off.

It was confirmed on November 20th that away supporters wanting to purchase a ticket for Blackburn's clash with Bolton could do so on a general sale basis, after those with 4,500 or more points on the club's loyalty scheme were given a two-day headstart.

Even if the journey is straightforward, those in the away end still had to part with a sizeable sum of cash, particularly if they are an adult-paying supporter.

Indeed, tickets in such brackets cost £36, whilst an adult wanting to take one junior supporter with them to the match still had to part with a combined £45 for the two tickets.

However, the aforementioned bundle was only available in the upper tier of the Toughsheet Community Stadium's away allocation.

This may come as little surprise too, as Bolton rank sixth in the Championship when it comes to the average price of a ticket for visiting supporters.

Given their recent four-point haul, Rovers now sit level with five other Championship sides in this particular metric, having taken 10 points from a possible 27 on the road.

Bolton, meanwhile, have failed to make their home ground the fortress it needs to be in order to consolidate, winning just two of their first nine matches at the Toughsheet.

Blackburn will look to pile on the misery in that regard, especially with the recent form displayed by Andri Gudjohnsen, whose father, Eidur, enjoyed two spells with the Whites.

By Seye Omidiora | 25 Nov 2026 02:12.

Argentine giants Boca Juniors are reportedly keen to bring Tottenham Hotspur midfielder Rodrigo Bentancur back to Buenos Aires as they prepare for next year's Copa Libertadores.

While funding a deal for the 29-year-old Uruguay international would normally prove difficult, the potential sale of highly rated youngster Milton Delgado could hand Boca the financial firepower required.

Aston Villa are among a host of English clubs tracking the 21-year-old defensive midfielder, meaning a winter raid from Unai Emery's side could directly threaten Tottenham's midfield depth.

According to Argentine outlets El Crack Deportivo and El Intransigente via Sport Witness, Boca president Juan Roman Riquelme has already started preliminary work on re-signing Bentancur.

Riquelme views the Spurs stalwart as his preferred candidate to replace Delgado should the academy graduate depart La Bombonera in the coming months.

Bentancur progressed through Boca's youth ranks before earning a switch to Juventus in 2017 and is seen as the ideal experienced presence to anchor their upcoming continental campaign.

The South American outfit strategy to reinvest the proceeds from Delgado's prospective transfer straight into a formal approach for their former player.

Delgado's stock has risen even further after he played the full 90 minutes in Boca's 2-0 Copa Sudamericana final triumph over Atletico Mineiro on Saturday.

Villa are reportedly preparing a formal January offer for Delgado after scouting the 21-year-old extensively across the past six months.

However, Emery's side are far from alone in the race, with Chelsea, Bournemouth, Brighton and West Ham United all linked with the youngster.

Boca are believed to have previously rejected a £7.5m bid from MLS side Atlanta United back in August, around the same time Chelsea and Bournemouth lodged initial enquiries for the young midfielder, who is valued at €10m (£8.4m) by Transfermarkt.

Portuguese outfit Porto are also believed to be monitoring developments from Europe, leaving Riquelme in a strong position to command a substantial fee if a bidding war erupts.

Even if Boca secure the necessary funds, convincing Bentancur to leave North London could prove complicated given that he signed a latest long-term contract with Tottenham in October 2025 and has spent almost a decade competing at the top level in Europe.

Frosinone head coach Massimiliano Alvini has admitted that his side simply gave AC Milan too many opportunities.

It has been a very positive return to the top flight for Frosinone so far, given that a point last night at San Siro would have seen them move back into the European places. However, they were ultimately given a bit of a humbling by Milan, who won 5-1 thanks to a ruthless counter-attacking display.

Industry observers note that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Some have questioned if the Canarini were a bit too aggressive in their approach to the game, given they played with such a high line and allowed space for Adrien Rabiot, Diego Moreira, Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic to exploit.

According to recent reports, alvini was present in the press conference room at San Siro after the full-time whistle and he analysed what was perhaps the most difficult night of the season for his team. MilanNews transcribed his assessments.

Should the game have been played differently?

Industry observers note that “Frosinone played their game but made a few mistakes they don’t usually make, but that’s certainly not my concern, losing by such a large margin. What’s worrying are the mistakes we made that we could have avoided.”.

Sources indicate that “We made a mistake on the first goal, which was a mistake of our own, while the other goals we conceded were goals we absolutely could have avoided. We conceded them and were naive.

“It’s a mistake of our own, and so today, from this perspective, if you come to Milan against Milan and make these mistakes, it’s only natural that we end up losing like this, by such a large scoreline.

“That’s the analysis, even though I think the scoreline is even too large: the first half, in my opinion, was extraordinary on our part.”.

Did the absences have an impact, forcing you to experiment a bit?

Sources indicate that “There’s nothing experimental about it. We played with the same principles, running forward to get to Rabiot. We preferred to bring on a defender who would push forward rather than a midfielder.

“In my opinion, this definitely didn’t influence the result, but rather the attitude, the idea, or the match strategy. And we certainly made – as I noted before and I’ll repeat – mistakes we don’t usually make.

“If you give Milan certain chances, with such strong players and the quality of this team, you risk losing, and that’s what happened. You risk losing with a heavy defeat, and that’s what happened.

In a recent development, “He had a problem with that back heel in the box, and he definitely needs tests. It’s too early now; we’ll have to wait for the tests, which will be done starting Tuesday, but it’s definitely a problem.”.

“We had a chance with Monterisi after a minute, we hit the post, and we created a lot. I have nothing to say to the team for their attitude and the way they played.

“We, I repeat, made some naivety, some mistakes. It’s also up to me to understand that there are crucial players on the other side who can cause problems.”.

“It’s a result that definitely needs to be managed, navigated, and channeled, but it doesn’t change my attitude at all. We have 20 points today. The path we need to take is to try to stay in Serie A, and we’ll try to do so with this attitude, with this identity: this is the path we’ll take.

Recent findings suggest that “Four years ago, I drew a game against Milan by playing defensively, and we took home a point. Today we made some mistakes, but this is the path we’ll take. I’m happier with the management, with the team’s identity, to try to achieve that objective, and this is what we’ll continue to do.”.

Southampton boss Tonda Eckert has confirmed he spoke to Middlesbrough boss Kim Hellberg in private ahead of the two clubs meeting for the first time since Spygate on Friday night.

As all football fans will remember from a story that dominated English football at the time, Saints were expelled from the play-offs after they admitted sending an employee to watch Boro train ahead of their play-off semi-final.

Therefore, despite losing to the south coast outfit over two legs, it was Middlesbrough who went to Wembley, although they did lose the final to Hull.

The punishment didn’t end there for Southampton, who admitted spying on several other Championship rivals earlier in the season, and they started the current campaign with a four-point deduction.

Recent findings suggest that given everything that had gone on, the first meeting between the two clubs was always going to be a spicy affair, and they face each other at St. Mary’s Stadium on Friday night, in a game that has been chosen for live TV coverage.

With Hellberg previously calling Southampton’s actions ‘disgraceful’, as well as stating what went on ‘breaks my heart’, the talking points ahead of the game were always going to extend beyond what happens on the pitch.

And, when asked about his relationship with Hellberg, Saints chief Eckert tried to play things down, as he revealed to journalist Alfie House that the pair did have discussions before the season started.

According to recent reports, “We've had a conversation on the phone and we saw each other at the EFL day before the season. We are two managers who will try to win a game and that's it.”.

You can understand Eckert’s comments here, and there’s no doubt that Hellberg will echo those words, as it’s all about trying to win the game.

Given everything that had gone on, the first time the two clubs met was always going to be a big deal though, and all eyes will be on the dugouts to see how the managers greet each other before kick-off.

But, both clubs are trying to move on from what happened, and, in some ways, they will just be glad to get this game out of the way, as a lot of the build-up and noise around the fixture is all based on last season.

Clearly, Middlesbrough were furious at what happened, but Saints will feel they were hit with a severe punishment, with the points deduction meaning they go into the game seven points behind Hellberg’s side, as opposed to three.

Ultimately, this is a huge game in the promotion race, and both clubs will know that they will be sending out a statement if they can emerge victorious.

Southampton have an exceptional home record this season, so they will fancy their chances, but a loss will leave a substantial gap to Boro in the battle for a top two finish.

Meanwhile, Middlesbrough know that Saints can apply real pressure to them with a win, and they risk dropping from first to fifth with a defeat on the south coast if results go against them this weekend.

So, there’s so much riding on this game in terms of the table, and that’s before you consider what a win could do for either side in helping them build momentum and to add to their confidence.

Serie A duo Como and Napoli are reportedly monitoring Manchester United forward Joshua Zirkzee ahead of the January transfer window.

The 25-year-old Netherlands international has struggled to secure regular playing time under multiple managers since arriving at Old Trafford from Bologna in the summer of 2024.

Zirkzee is yet to make a single Premier League start during the 2026-27 campaign, with all seven of his top-flight outings coming from the substitutes' bench.

After nearly leaving England on Deadline Day, when United rejected an approach from Everton, the attacker could now be set for a winter return to Italian football.

The forward has been earmarked as a possible early departure from Old Trafford under Mauricio Pochettino in January.

No formal negotiations have been opened with the Red Devils hierarchy yet as suitors wait to discover whether the Argentine tactician considers the forward surplus to requirements.

Zirkzee has managed two goals across his limited substitute appearances this season, netting against Aston Villa in the league and ironically finding the back of the net against Como in the Champions League last month.

The Dutchman's previous pedigree in Italy, where he earned a spot in the Serie A Team of the Year with Bologna, ensures his stock remains high across the peninsula despite his Old Trafford struggles.

Both interested sides have urgent attacking voids to fill when the winter market opens for business.

Como boss Cesc Fabregas recently confirmed that striker Moise Kean faces several months on the sidelines after aggravating a recurring tibia issue in training.

Meanwhile, Napoli boss Massimiliano Allegri is seeking fresh firepower after Lorenzo Lucca struggled to make an impact following his return from a loan spell at Nottingham Forest.

Bolton Wanderers boss Steven Schumacher simply doesn't know how significant a budget he'll be able to work with in the January transfer window, despite knowing where in the squad he wants to strengthen.

Industry observers note that the Trotters have had an okay start to life back in the Championship after a seven-year absence. Last season's League One play-off winners' main goal would have been to stay in the division, and thus far, they've remained above the dotted line.

Bolton sit 19th, with 18 points in 17 games. They've picked up some big wins, especially away from home, but are struggling at the Toughsheet Stadium and have only strung together back-to-back victories once.

It has been revealed that at the moment, it's just one win in seven, with losses against out-of-form Bristol City and Derby County in that time, both of which saw them lead. It almost feels as if they're looking to get through the next month to assess, and then kick on in January.

However, with the winter window still a month away, Steven Schumacher is just focusing on picking up points between now and then.

Bolton haven't spent a weekend inside the relegation zone as yet, and will hope to put some more distance between them and the bottom three before January. But that hasn't stopped him from asking some early questions regarding recruitment come the new year.

"It’s in the very early stages from my point of view,” the Bolton boss noted, per The Bolton News.

According to recent reports, "The lads are obviously in the recruitment office, and they are working hard. Every time I see Jimmy Dickinson or Owen (Davies – lead recruitment and data analyst) or Fergal (Harkin, director of football), I'm asking if they've got any players for us, and the answer they keep saying is: ‘We'll tell you later!’.

"So, we are focusing on the games for the time being, but that will start ramping up again in the next few weeks.".

Only Lincoln City are estimated to have a lower wage bill than Bolton this season, so it's a credit to Schumacher for keeping the Trotters competitive while still trying to play an entertaining, attacking brand of football.

Sources indicate that there's still obvious room for improvement, though, and Schumacher knows where they need to strengthen. The question is, though, how much money will be available for them to do so?

"I have spoken to Fergal and Owen, and we are very clear about areas of the team that we would like to strengthen," he continued.

"Whether we can do or not, I don't know. But, yeah, we'll be positive that when we get to January, we'll be in a good place, because the recruitment lads work hard, and they'll do their best.".

While Schumacher is remaining upbeat about the club's situation heading into January and the prospect of adding more quality, Bolton fans are a little more pessimistic regarding the fact that their head coach doesn't yet know how much will be available for him.

The Trotters endured a bit of a frustrating summer transfer window regarding player recruitment, especially in the forward areas.

Industry observers note that their pursuits of both Max Dean and Johnny Kenny fell flat, and while it allowed Sam Dalby to become an unexpected hero at the top end of the pitch, it didn't mask their annoyance at the lack of investment in the summer. Now, warning bells are ringing again.

According to recent reports, "League 1 it is, then. It's obvious the club doesn't want to back the manager," one fan said in response to the Bolton News article on X. "Good manager being let down," another added, while a third claimed that Schumacher was being "set up to fail.".

"It’s obvious a step up in the budget and therefore quality of recruitment is needed in January," was also among the replies, with frustrations being aired at the number of unproven, young arrivals at the club in the summer.

And one, quite plainly, wrote, "We don’t invest we’re goin down it’s as simple as that.".

Bolton have scrapped well in the Championship this season, all things considered, but when the January window opens, and sides around them with more lucrative budgets improve their squad, Wanderers need to be wary of possibly being left behind.

Preston North End are already starting to make ground and can even climb out of the drop zone this weekend, and those below them, Burnley and Derby, should have the funds to try and drag themselves out of this hot water they're in.

How important do you think the January window will be in Bolton's attempts to stay in the Championship? Let us know in the comments.

If they get better, and Bolton continue operating at around a point per game, they may not have enough to avoid an immediate drop back to League One, which would be a massive shame, given the potential of the club under Schumacher and the crowds they can attract.

We'll see what the Trotters do during January, but it's already becoming apparent amongst some sections of the supporter base that their winter dealings could define their season.

There are few transfers that get West Ham supporters talking quite like the sale of an academy graduate.

Who can forget the uproar after Grady Diangana joined West Brom in 2020, when club captain Mark Noble released a public statement voicing his anger and disappointment at the move.

Noble’s thoughts were echoed by team-mates at the time, while supporters were similarly up in arms at the sale of the winger.

So, when Freddie Potts joined Club Brugge for £10million on the eve of the season to mark the controversial departure of another product of the proclaimed Academy of Football, you can imagine the reaction.

According to recent reports, potts represented more than a graduate. A boyhood West Ham fan whose dad Steve is a club legend and still serves as a first-team coach, he joined the academy aged six. His brother Dan also came through the ranks.

The midfielder had just enjoyed a breakthrough campaign despite West Ham’s relegation, and many felt he was the perfect player to build their Championship promotion push around.

Freddie Potts is shining in Belgium with Club Brugge after joining from West Ham in the summer.

Potts joined the Hammers academy aged six and enjoyed a breakthrough year last season.

Hammers favourites Kevin Nolan and Tony Cottee weighed in with their disapproval at his sale, while celebrity fan Ray Winstone expressed his shock and anger live on talkSPORT.

‘Of course you see it (the division about the move) on social media,’ Potts tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘Every player does. But even though last season was tough I always felt I had a connection with the West Ham fans.

Industry observers note that ‘No matter if I played well or bad I always felt I understood what it meant to play for West Ham. It's a great club with great fans and people. In the end, I had to do what was best for me. I wanted to play this season, and I felt like this was the best place to do that.’.

Potts, 22 at the time of his exit, admits it was extremely tough and emotional for him and his family to leave a club he had been at for 16 years.

But, during pre-season he became aware he wasn’t likely to play as much as he wanted to under Nuno Espirito Santo.

In a recent development, ‘In the end it’s the manager’s decision,’ Potts claims. ‘I wasn’t getting the minutes I wanted. The feeling was that I wasn’t guaranteed to be in the looks as much as Club Brugge were promising me, so I thought it was best for me to move.

According to recent reports, ‘It was very hard. West Ham have been my club my whole life and I have a lot of love for West Ham. But I had to take into account what was best for my career and I’m loving it at Brugge. It’s a really exciting place full of great people and a great manager.’.

Potts had multiple options in the summer, including Premier League interest, yet the chance to play in the Champions League and compete for titles with Brugge attracted him.

Their record of developing young players and a talented squad that includes the likes of Carlos Forbs and Nicolo Tresoldi was equally compelling, and the midfielder hasn't looked back.

Potts started Brugge’s first 10 league games, missing their final one before the international break due to suspension. He returned at the weekend as they thrashed Mechelen 5-1. Ivan Leko’s side are one point adrift of Union Saint-Gilloise at the top of the Belgian Pro League, and they have also impressed in the Champions League.

It has been revealed that in Europe, Brugge have beaten Inter Milan, PSV and Lens on their way to nine points from 12, only narrowly losing 3-2 to Aston Villa. Potts has started each match, including their memorable 4-3 win against Inter at the San Siro, and they host Liverpool on Wednesday.

Sources indicate that ‘It's a really good group of lads,’ he states. ‘Everyone speaks English as well which helps me. It's a good team and we're happy playing with each other.’.

Industry observers note that he is clearly enjoying life and is just the fifth English player in history to play for the club. Potts did take time to settle though, and admits he initially suffered from homesickness.

In a recent development, ‘I found it difficult because East London and Essex have been my home for my whole life,’ he claims. ‘West Ham was my life. It was tough in terms of moving into a new language and everything but you get used to it and I’m really enjoying it here. It’ll be strange going back home to England.'.

Potts has been a regular and has had a key role in Brugge's impressive early exploits in Europe.

Brugge have beaten PSV, Lens and Inter Milan, and they take on Liverpool this Wednesday.

Recent findings suggest that potts’ family have popped over to see him and he has enjoyed exploring his new surroundings. He is yet to learn the local language and scolds himself for being lazy for relying on English, although he has picked up little bits of Flemish.

He has immersed himself in the culture too, and reveals he has tried the world-famous Belgian fries and a few local beers, albeit only when he has enough time to recover between games.

Despite his new life in Europe, Potts remains a West Ham fan and tries to watch them on TV every week.

According to recent reports, he has been surprised by their struggles on their return to the Championship for the first time in 14 years, with Nuno paying the price by losing his job. Former Hammers midfielder Scott Parker has since taken the reins.

According to recent reports, ‘I still think they're playing well,’ Potts says. ‘They've got a great team and Scott Parker is a really good manager. You get ups and downs but I still 100 per cent think West Ham will get promoted this year.'.

Potts’ stay in the Hammers first team may have been brief, yet there were still plenty of highs, not least a storming performance on his first Premier League start. That came in a win over Newcastle last November in the Hammers’ first home victory of the season. He was also coached by his dad, an experience he jokes had positives and negatives.

He left West Ham after realising he was unlikely to be first choice under Nuno Espirito Santo.

Potts is a boyhood West Ham fan and is fully expecting them to get promoted this season.

Attention now turns to Brugge’s clash against Liverpool. It promises to be a tricky challenge for Andoni Iraola’s side against a team who are determined to prove themselves on the European stage.

The two teams are level on points in the league phase, and Potts is keen for his side to take another scalp.

‘I don't think there's much difference in the way we've been performing in the Champions League,’ Potts concludes. ‘It'll be difficult for them to come to our place as well.

In recent seasons, Manu Kone has often been linked with Paris Saint-Germain, but the capital club have never really tried to sign him. The reason behind that choice has been revealed.

A talented French international from the Paris region, Manu Kone seemed to have the ideal profile to join PSG. The Roma midfielder has often been reported on the capital club's shortlist, but PSG have never really tried to recruit him.

The 25-year-old will return to the Parc des Princes on Wednesday at 8pm UK time, for matchday five of the Champions League with the Italian side.

He will have the chance to show the full extent of his talent to Parisian supporters, although it is unlikely that Kone will join the two-time European champions in the short term, according to L'Equipe.

The sports daily tried to explain the reasons for PSG's choice not to sign the French midfielder. This summer, Paris simply had no desire to recruit another midfielder and wanted to count on their current squad, with its established players such as Vitinha and Joao Neves, and its young gems such as Dro Fernandez and Senny Mayulu.

It has been revealed that paris had an opportunity in the summer of 2024. Before his move to Roma for £15.3m (€18m), the Frenchman was offered to Paris. Some people internally pushed for the capital club to sign this promising and affordable young box-to-box midfielder. Luis Campos has always liked the profile of the former Toulouse player.

However, PSG decided otherwise. 'I do not make all the decisions on my own' - the Paris sporting director said.

L'Equipe concludes that Luis Enrique did not approve the option. The Spanish boss preferred to rely on his Neves-Vitinha-Ruiz trio. Therefore, unless he changes his mind, the Kone option appears to be one to forget in Paris.

While PSG appear to have moved on, Kone has regularly been linked with clubs in England. Chelsea, Liverpool and Manchester United were all credited with interest in the Roma midfielder during the summer transfer window, including on deadline day, according to the Liverpool Echo.

In a recent development, chelsea were noted to still have an interest in late August, with Kone one of several midfielders on their list, according to CaughtOffside. At that stage, the website considered Manchester United effectively out of the race after the signings of Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba, although that was its own assessment rather than a reported club position.

Recent findings suggest that more recently, Gazzetta dello Sport reported in mid-November that Chelsea could make a move in January. Roma boss Gian Piero Gasperini reportedly vetoed a sale in the final hours of the summer window, and the Italian club are said to value Kone at £47m-£51m (€55m-€60m), compared with the £43m reported in August.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lincoln City are on the hunt for a third managerial figure this calendar year following the midweek decision to part ways with joint-managers, Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw.

The duo led the Imps into their first Championship season since 1961 following Michael Skubala's summer exit to divisional rivals, Bristol City.

Lincoln coasted to last season's League One title, accumulating a staggering 103 points whilst also embarking on a 29-match unbeaten run.

But as the final month of 2026 nears, they are the lowest-placed out of the three sides who earned promotion last term, having taken just 15 points from their first 17 matches.

It remains to be seen which direction is taken by owner, Ron Fowler at the ProAmpac Stadium, but it has emerged that a previous target, now working with another Championship club, has entered the managerial frame.

Lincoln are right now outside the relegation zone by three points, with Tuesday's heavy 4-0 defeat to Charlton Athletic at The Valley, coupled with the manner of their side's performance, spelt the end for Cohen and Shaw.

The Imps have won just one of their last six Championship matches, with it now emerging through Alan Nixon - via Patreon - that Gavin Strachan has been listed as a potential candidate.

Strachan, 47, is presently on the coaching staff at West Bromwich Albion under James Morrison, with the Baggies currently within three points of the Championship summit after a 3-1 win at Bolton Wanderers.

Prior to the start of the newly introduced season, the Aberdeen-born man spent six years at Celtic working under the likes of Brendan Rodgers, Ange Postecoglou and Martin O'Neill, with the Hoops winning the last five Scottish Premiership titles on offer.

Following on from Postecoglou's exit to Tottenham Hotspur three years ago, the Australian wished to take Strachan with him to North London, but a deal could not be agreed.

The aforementioned Morrison was appointed as permanent head coach of West Brom this summer after ensuring the Black Country side's survival in difficult circumstances.

As well as retaining Matt Gill, who had been linked with a switch to Leicester City, the former Scotland international midfielder opted to install Strachan and Tony McMahon as part of a newly introduced-look coaching setup.

Given how highly Strachan is rated on the coaching circuit, Morrison's initial words following the decision read: "I’m also delighted to add Gavin Strachan to the group.

According to recent reports, "Having a newly introduced pair of eyes from somebody with Gavin’s experience will help us massively. He has worked alongside some top managers, like Martin O’Neill, Ange Postecoglou and Brendan Rodgers, and will no doubt bring fresh ideas with him.".

Prior to his spell with Celtic, Strachan also assisted Darren Ferguson in two spells at Peterborough United, as well as his stint with Doncaster Rovers.

The decision for the Imps to remove Cohen and Shaw from their positions as joint-managers was the sixth managerial change already made in this season's Championship.

Four of those have been made by clubs in a similar region of the table to Lincoln, with Watford, Burnley and Preston North End all replacing Alessio Dionisi, Nicky Hayen and Paul Heckingbottom with Edward Iordanescu, Fabio Celestini and Graham Alexander respectively.

Industry observers note that lincoln fans, would Gavin Strachan be a wise appointment at this particular moment? Comment below!

With the Reds needing to rediscover form, particularly on home turf, in a bid to survive against the odds, supporters will be hoping that the board get their next decision right.

However, it has already been confirmed that no final call will be made ahead of Saturday's daunting task of taking on Wolves, with Shaun Pearson taking interim charge.

The first South Wales derby between Swansea City and Cardiff City for just short of two years takes place on Sunday, and clarity has been provided regarding the hosts' search for a new head coach.

Swansea started the Championship campaign in fine fettle, leading the division as recently as October 17th under Vitor Matos, who then made the decision to join RC Strasbourg, much to the bemusement of those in South Wales.

The Portuguese was only installed as Alan Sheehan's replacement 12 months ago, winning 22 of his 47 matches in charge, with the last of those being the late loss at Birmingham City on November 7th.

Within a rather frosty announcement by the Welsh side, it was confirmed that Kris O'Leary, Ashley Williams, Joe Allen and Leon Britton were to lead the 2-2 draw against West Bromwich Albion last weekend, before also overseeing Tuesday's 2-1 loss to league leaders, Middlesbrough.

With ownership duo, Brett Cravatt and Jason Cohen, seeking a swift replacement, clarity has now been provided as to who will lead the Swans for the weekend's grudge match against the Bluebirds.

Despite a recent dip in form, Swansea are narrowly outside the early-season play-off places, and, if results fall their way in the next 72 hours, they could return to the top eight.

The club's current situation has led to intense speculation over who could take the reins, with Rob Edwards and Tommy Elphick initially linked, before reports emerged over the potential hire of Rosenborg boss, Freyr Alexandersson.

Alexandersson's current employers are right now fourth in the Norwegian Eliteserien and have three matches to play in a bid to secure European qualification.

Despite the 44-year-old acknowledging such links, it has been revealed by Sky Sports' Anthony Joseph that the quartet of Williams, O'Leary, Britton and Allen will take charge against Cardiff, and, potentially, the three subsequent fixtures as Alexandersson may see out the remainder of the campaign at the Lerkendal Stadion.

Unsurprisingly, the fact Swansea may now have to wait at least two more weeks for full clarity on who takes the long-term reins in the dugout has sparked an immediate reaction.

Sources indicate that one of many responses read: "Whilst the derby was always going to be a bit of a push. We can't wait until 13th, that's another 4 games and a significant amount of points on the table and then to ask him to settle over christmas period. It has to be now or never for me.".

Another wrote: "If we have to wait until 13th December, move on.".

"Will be like when we persisted with Sheehan last season, need a newly introduced manager in asap," noted another Swans fan.

"Potentially another 4 games in charge before we hire a upcoming manager is bonkers," backed up the general feeling amongst the fanbase.

Another fan gave an in-depth stance on the matter, replying: "Waiting until mid-December to make an appointment is potentially catastrophic for our season, especially when waiting for a manager with a completely unproven track record. December is the busiest stretch of the season, it’s not a month that you can afford to throw away.".

Swans fans, how are you feeling about this enhancement ahead of the South Wales derby? Comment below!

However, some took a more philosophical outlook, with one comment reading: "The right appointment is the much better option than the quick appointment. Fans moaned on here the other day when it seemed he'd walk out on Rosenborg as he would be "another Matos" to us and leave us swiftly. Now they moan he isn't leaving them in the lurch. You have to laugh.".

Whilst uncertainty on the managerial front could be a hindrance for Swansea, especially with games against Bristol City, Bolton Wanderers and Charlton Athletic on the horizon potentially before a decision is made, in the short-term, the presence of Williams and Co. on the touchline may be a major benefit against Cardiff.

With the quartet boasting over 1,200 appearances for the club, they are aware, more than most, of how much this derby means to the locals, especially having lost the last meeting to a Bluebirds side who were ultimately relegated in rock-bottom to League One.

It also remains to be seen whether an upturn in form lands the Wales assistant a chance of the permanent role, but that will not be on Williams' mind right now.

Real Madrid produced a sensational second-half comeback to beat PSV Eindhoven 5-1 in the Champions League on Tuesday evening, with England star Jude Bellingham proving instrumental after being introduced at half-time.

According to recent reports, jose Mourinho's side were trailing 1-0 at the interval following Ivan Perisic's penalty, but Federico Valverde restored parity before the 23-year-old produced a spectacular volley to put Los Blancos ahead. Kylian Mbappe scored twice, and Vinicius Junior added a fifth to complete the turnaround.

Bellingham's influence attracted widespread praise from the Spanish media, with several publications describing him as the decisive figure in Madrid's transformation.

His 45-minute contribution included a goal, an assist and a series of impressive individual statistics.

AS were particularly impressed, publishing the headline "Bellingham: lo cambio todo" - 'Bellingham changed everything'.

Manu de Juan highlighted how the England international reorganised Madrid's midfield, allowing Arda Guler to operate deeper and giving the hosts greater control and attacking momentum. AS also praised his spectacular volley for the 2-1 lead and his subsequent assist for Vinicius.

El Pais delivered perhaps the most glowing assessment, publishing the headline "El esplendor deslumbrante de Bellingham impulsa la goleada del Madrid al PSV" - Bellingham's 'dazzling brilliance' drives Madrid's thrashing of PSV.

Industry observers note that david Alvarez argued that Madrid's first-half performance had been lifeless and directionless, with Bellingham's introduction restoring clarity, composure and quality. His spectacular volley was described as a beautiful and devastating goal, with the newspaper suggesting the Englishman's arrival completely transformed the contest.

Mundo Deportivo labelled Bellingham a "superestrella" - 'superstar' - and suggested that he is at the moment Madrid's best player, while highlighting how his introduction changed the game.

It has been revealed that elDesmarque were equally enthusiastic, awarding the midfielder 9/10 and naming him their MVP. They highlighted his immediate influence, spectacular goal and assist for Vinicius, describing his 45 minutes as an outstanding exhibition.

Real Madrid-focused publications Defensa Central and madridistaReal went even further, awarding him 10/10 and 9.5/10 respectively. Both considered his introduction the turning point in Madrid's victory.

Spanish radio station Cadena SER also marvelled at his volley, with several commentators comparing the technical brilliance of the finish to something Zinedine Zidane might have produced - 'It's like Zizou,' one remarked.

Mourinho was equally impressed, describing the England international's performance as "absolutamente devastador" - 'absolutely devastating'.

The Portuguese coach explained that he had initially considered leaving Bellingham out to protect him from fatigue, believing Madrid could win without him. However, he admitted that having the midfielder available from the bench proved decisive.

Mourinho also described Bellingham as a different type of player who provided something Madrid had been missing during the opening 45 minutes.

Recent findings suggest that the statistics underline why the praise was justified. Despite playing just 45 minutes, Bellingham registered one goal, one assist and created three chances. According to Sofascore, he also completed 100% of his attempted dribbles, won all of his tackles and claimed 75% of his duels.

His influence extended beyond the spectacular finish, with his movement between the lines helping Madrid establish control and create opportunities for their forwards.

There is little doubt that Bellingham was the defining figure in Madrid's comeback - while Mourinho's triple half-time substitution and improved collective pressing also played key roles, the Englishman's ability to bring structure, energy and creativity to the midfield was particularly striking.

It has been revealed that receiving such glowing praise from the Spanish media and his manager after just 45 minutes illustrates the level Bellingham can reach when operating at his best. His goal may have been the highlight, but it was his all-round contribution that made this one of his most impressive performances of the season.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Middlesbrough midfielder Myles Peart-Harris has said the Boro squad are "excited" for a "massive game" against Southampton on the South Coast on Friday night.

Sources indicate that it's the first meeting between the two sides since the play-off semi-final last season, which Spygate ultimately overshadowed. Ahead of the first leg, Boro officials caught a Saints analyst illegally spying on their training session.

Industry observers note that the games went ahead, and Southampton prevailed in extra time after neither side could be separated in 180 minutes. However, the EFL would then expel Tonda Eckert's side from the play-off final and reinstate Middlesbrough to take on Hull City at Wembley.

Sources indicate that since the Tigers beat Boro in May, the rivalry between both fanbases has been brewing, and was stoked by Eckert being handed just a fine and a suspended sentence by the FA for his role in the operation last month. A week ago, the German was given a latest contract at St Mary's.

Fans of clubs can often play down the importance of games, or brand something as "their cup final, not ours," when discussing a matchup between two new rivals, but deep down, both Southampton and Middlesbrough fans want to get one over each other on Friday night.

Peart-Harris, who took his chance back in the starting eleven for the first time in two months on Tuesday night with a goal and an assist in the 2-1 win over Swansea City, watched on from home as Spygate played out back in May, given he wasn't at the club.

However, the 24-year-old knows how much the game means on Friday, and is looking forward to being a part of it.

"Everyone was watching it [the spygate developments]," he said, per the Northern Echo. "I remember watching the semi-final, and then I think maybe a week later you hear the news about what happened. So now, it's definitely something I’m excited to be a part of.

"Friday's a massive game. It’s a massive football game before anything else, but the rivalry that we now have makes it even better.".

On how the rest of the team feels heading into the game, a lot of them will be looking to pick up a major win to almost right the wrongs of the last time they were down at St Mary's in the play-off semi-finals.

In a recent development, "The boys are looking forward to Friday. Hopefully we go down there, and we play our football, we stick to what we know and get a result," he continued.

In a recent development, "We're ready, and we’re excited. I think we're just more excited about the game of football that's going to actually happen, because we know they like to play football, we like to play football, so I think tactically it's going to be a great game for everyone to watch.

"Our aim will be to go down and just get a win.".

As Peart-Harris said, first and foremost, though, Friday night will be a great chance for two of the best sides in the division to go head-to-head.

Kim Hellberg and Tonda Eckert are widely regarded as two of the brightest up-and-coming coaches in the game, and in the past year since they both took over at their respective clubs, the brand of football being played has been fascinating to watch.

This season, Boro have picked up 35 points, while Southampton have collected 32, albeit the four-point deduction handed to them in the wake of the Spygate charges by the EFL means that they sit on 28, seven points adrift of their visitors on Friday.

Sources indicate that who do you think comes out on top on Friday? Let us know in the comments.

The Teessiders have a tough task on their hands, with Eckert's side utterly dominant at home this season. The only side to have come away with any points from St Mary's through eight games were Bolton Wanderers, who needed to rely on a good defensive display to grind out a 0-0 draw.

In a recent development, it'll be intriguing to see if Boro set up any differently to help combat an unstoppable force on their home patch. Either way, these two teams, and both managers, are destined for the Premier League, and it'll be fun to see them lock horns for the first time this season.

Ultimately, this brooding rivalry is more to do with those in the stands, and perhaps the two coaches in the dugouts, too, even if both have since buried the hatchet after the incident back in May.

It has been revealed that the Southampton players who were there to play out the semi-final in the play-offs last season likely weren't to know what Eckert and co were doing to help prepare them for games, and aren't really to blame. Taylor Harwood-Bellis, who was the pantomime villain, mocking Aidan Morris with a spy celebration after Shea Charles' winner, is no longer at the club.

They will be emotionally charged by the atmosphere inside St Mary's on Friday, though, which will have a little more of an edge to it. As mentioned earlier, both sets of fans may pretend not to care, but they do, deep down.

A red-hot atmosphere and two good footballing sides should create a wonderful cocktail of Championship football, and if both teams are up for it, it could go down as one of the games of the season already.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

From Diego Forlan’s unforgettable double to Juan Mata’s spectacular volley, Manchester United have enjoyed some memorable victories at Anfield over the years.

With Mauricio Pochettino preparing for his first match in charge against Liverpool on Sunday, we look back at five occasions when United emerged victorious from one of English football’s fiercest fixtures.

United travelled to Anfield on 19 April 1997 knowing Liverpool could overtake them at the top of the Premier League with a victory. Instead, centre-back Gary Pallister scored twice with headers from David Beckham deliveries, either side of John Barnes’s equaliser.

In a recent development, andy Cole added a third after the interval, heading home from Gary Neville’s cross following an error by Liverpool goalkeeper David James. The victory helped Sir Alex Ferguson’s side take a decisive step towards retaining the Premier League title, which they secured the following month.

In a recent development, fresh from winning the Treble, United returned to Anfield for a remarkable match in September 1999. Jamie Carragher headed into his own net inside three minutes before Andy Cole doubled United’s advantage.

Recent findings suggest that sami Hyypia pulled a goal back for Liverpool, but Carragher’s second own goal restored the visitors’ two-goal lead. Patrik Berger reduced the deficit again, and United faced a difficult finish after Cole was sent off for a second bookable offence. Despite playing the closing stages with 10 men, Ferguson’s side held on for a 3-2 victory.

In a recent development, diego Forlan had endured a frustrating start to his United career before producing a performance that supporters would remember for years. The Uruguayan opened the scoring after Liverpool goalkeeper Jerzy Dudek failed to gather the ball, allowing him to finish from close range.

Forlan added a second just minutes later, beating Dudek at his near post to put United in control. Sami Hyypia pulled one back for Liverpool, but Ferguson’s side held on for a victory that proved valuable in their successful pursuit of the 2002-03 Premier League title. Forlan’s double also inspired a terrace song that remains familiar to United supporters.

Few United victories at Anfield have been as dramatic as the one secured by John O’Shea in March 2007. Liverpool had enjoyed the better opportunities, and United’s task became harder when Paul Scholes was sent off late in the second half.

It has been revealed that with a goalless draw appearing increasingly likely, Cristiano Ronaldo’s free-kick was parried by goalkeeper Pepe Reina. Substitute O’Shea reacted quickest, firing the rebound high into the net in stoppage time. The unexpected winner gave United three valuable points on their way to reclaiming the Premier League title.

Juan Mata produced one of the most memorable individual performances in this fixture during Louis van Gaal’s first season as United manager. The Spaniard opened the scoring after 14 minutes, finishing a move involving Ander Herrera, before doubling United’s lead with a spectacular scissor-kick volley after half-time.

In a recent development, liverpool captain Steven Gerrard had been sent off just 38 seconds after coming on as a substitute at the interval. Daniel Sturridge reduced the deficit, while Wayne Rooney missed a late penalty, but United held on for a 2-1 victory. Mata’s second goal remains one of the outstanding moments of United’s Premier League visits to Anfield.

Sources indicate that those five victories underline the different ways United have succeeded at Anfield, from outstanding individual performances to late winners and determined defensive displays. Pochettino now has an opportunity to begin his managerial reign with a memorable result against United’s biggest rivals.

Which United victory at Anfield is your favourite? Were you there for Forlan’s double, O’Shea’s winner or Mata’s volley? Share your memories in the comments below.

Tech Report: Transfer news: Major Saudi Pro League rule change could shake up the market

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (573 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Axel Clody | 25 Nov 2026 07:26.
  • With a little over a month to go until the transfer window reopens, clubs around the world are already moving behind the scenes to strengthen their squads.
  • According to The Times, the Saudi Pro League (SPL) is considering raising the limit on foreign players ahead of the 2027-28 window, which could trigger a new wave of signings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 25 Nov 2026 07:26.

With a little over a month to go until the transfer window reopens, clubs around the world are already moving behind the scenes to strengthen their squads. Saudi Arabia, which has become a leading player in the market in recent years, is considering a change that could boost its domestic league but worry other countries.

According to The Times, the Saudi Pro League (SPL) is considering raising the limit on foreign players ahead of the 2027-28 window, which could trigger a new wave of signings. Saudi clubs are seeking clarification on the matter before the Northern Hemisphere winter window in January.

In a recent development, at present, clubs in Saudi Arabia can register up to eight foreign players in a 25-man squad, with the option of adding two more foreign under-21 players for SPL matches. The idea is to raise that limit to 14 or more, with discussions still ongoing.

It has been revealed that should the newly introduced rule come into force, Saudi clubs are likely to make more international signings. That could mark a new phase of departures from Europe to join the Saudi project, which aims to improve the competitive level of local football before the country hosts the World Cup in 2034.

In January 2023, Cristiano Ronaldo joined Al-Nassr after terminating his contract with Manchester United, which began a series of Saudi investments in football. In June of that year, the Public Investment Fund (PIF) took control of the four biggest domestic clubs: Al-Ahli, Al-Hilal, Al-Ittihad and Al-Nassr, the Portuguese star's team.

Then Ballon d'Or winner Karim Benzema was another high-profile name to leave Real Madrid for the Saudi Pro League, followed by stars such as N'Golo Kante and Roberto Firmino. Over the past three seasons, Neymar, Ollie Watkins, Gabriel Martinelli, Tijjani Reijnders, Darwin Nunez, Ivan Toney, Sadio Mane and Joao Felix have also been tempted by the Middle East.

As well as drawing global attention to its league, Saudi Arabia believes the move has helped the development of its homegrown talent. Competing for starting places with foreign stars encourages local players to improve.

On the other hand, critics of the proposal to raise the limit on non-Saudi players argue that the rule change could force local players to move abroad, or even leave bigger clubs for smaller ones, in order to get playing time.

Industry observers note that it is worth remembering that the PIF has reduced its international sports investments, to the point of ending its backing of LIV Golf. In April, the fund announced a five-year programme with a greater focus on domestic investment. Privatisations of Saudi clubs have also been recurring, such as the sale of 70 per cent of Al-Hilal in August.

According to recent reports, because of the geopolitical context in the region, including Saudi Arabia's conflict with the Yemen-based Houthi rebels, there is some uncertainty over the league's ability to attract foreign players in the short term. In October, the airport in the capital, Riyadh, was hit by a missile attack that killed 13 people and injured more than 300.

The Asian Cup, which was due to be held in the country between January and February 2027, was postponed earlier this month. Three SPL matches were also postponed after the October Houthi attacks, although organisers did not attribute the decision to the conflict, saying it was motivated by 'logistical considerations'.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Senegal have been reinstated as Africa Cup of Nations winners after succeeding with an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), ten months after they beat Morocco in Rabat.
  • The ruling follows a controversial final in which Senegal initially won 1-0 after extra time, only for the result to be overturned following an appeal to Confederation of African Football (CAF) by the Moroccan Football Federation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 09:30 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 14:47 EST, 24 November 2026.

Senegal have been reinstated as Africa Cup of Nations winners after succeeding with an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), ten months after they beat Morocco in Rabat.

The ruling follows a controversial final in which Senegal initially won 1-0 after extra time, only for the result to be overturned following an appeal to Confederation of African Football (CAF) by the Moroccan Football Federation.

Two months after the final, the CAF appeal board ruled that Senegal had forfeited the match because their players had walked off the pitch in protest over a controversial penalty decision.

Morocco were subsequently awarded a 3-0 victory and the title. Despite that, Senegal refused to hand the trophy over.

That decision was based on Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON regulations, which state that leaving the pitch constitutes a forfeit.

However, following an appeal to CAS, Senegal have been reinstalled as champions, with the court ruling that FIFA's law that the referee’s decision is final takes precedence over the competition regulations.

Therefore, because the officials did not enforce the competition regulations at the time, there were no grounds to overturn the result.

The Moroccan FA, though, have not given up and have vowed to take the matter beyond CAS after questioning the integrity of panelist Ulrich Haas.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport has restored Senegal as Africa Cup of Nations winners after they were successful in their appeal.

Morocco were awarded a 3-0 victory two months after the final, after it was ruled Senegal had forfeited the match by walking off the pitch in protest over a late penalty decision.

Senegal fans clashed with security in Rabat after the controversial penalty decision.

Ruling in favour of Senegal on Tuesday, CAS said: 'In the Panel’s view, there is no doubt that the effects of the Referee’s decision were limited to the pitch.

'As such, the Panel considers that the Referee’s decision was covered by the "field of play" doctrine.

'Since Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations are intended solely to determine the outcome of a match when a team’s conduct leads the referee to call off the game permanently, they are therefore not applicable in this case.'.

A statement from the Moroccan FA later added: 'We take note of the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport regarding the appeal filed by the Senegalese Football Federation against the decision of the CAF Appeals Committee, relating to the final match of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations. In this context, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation expresses its surprise and protest at the failure to take into account its demand to arrange the necessary legal consequences for practices that would compromise the integrity and credibility of the arbitration procedure, especially what has been confirmed regarding communication between the German referee Ulrich Haas (who sat on the CAS panel) and the president of the Senegalese Football Federation, 48 hours before the decision was issued.

'The Royal Moroccan Football Federation also notes that the decision did not take into account the approach recently adopted by both the International Football Association Board (IFAB) and FIFA, regarding players leaving the field of play without the referee’s permission, and the resulting disciplinary responsibilities and penalties.

'Accordingly, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation confirms its intention to pursue all available legal avenues to appeal the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport.'.

The chaos was triggered by events at the end of normal time, when referee Jean Jacques Ndala awarded Morocco a contentious penalty in the 98th minute after being called to the monitor by the video assistant referee to review El Hadji Malick Diouf’s challenge on Brahim Diaz.

The decision came just minutes after Senegal had seen a goal ruled out.

Furious with the penalty decision, Senegal manager Pape Thiaw instructed his players to leave the pitch in protest.

After a 17-minute delay, the team eventually returned, with former Liverpool forward Sadio Mane earning praise for remaining on the pitch and encouraging his teammates to continue.

In the dramatic aftermath, Real Madrid forward Brahim Diaz saw his Panenka penalty stopped by Senegal goalkeeper Edouard Mendy, before Ndala brought normal time to an end.

Senegal went on to score early in extra time, which has now led to a second title in the past three editions of the tournament with their 1-0 victory eventually confirmed in the courtroom.

It would be with the Potters where he would play the most games in his career, making 173 appearances across all competitions in North Staffordshire, having joined the club from Portsmouth in January 2010 for around £3.25 million, and eventually being sold to Chelsea for around £8 million.

Speaking to The Sentinel, the Bosnian has been full of praise for current Stoke number one and Sweden international Viktor Johansson, saying: "I think he certainly does have Premier League potential. I think you can see now he's being very selective with his next move. I think he wants to continue to play.

"I'm sure he would have had opportunities to go in as a number two at times, but I think the fact that he wants to play and be number one for club and country shows a lot about his character and his mentality. I think he definitely has the capabilities and talent to play in the Premier League.".

Johansson penned a fresh four-year deal at the bet365 Stadium over the summer, having initially joined the club from Rotherham United in the summer of 2024 for just over £1 million, and has been exceptional ever since.

Certainly, Johansson will be hoping to play Premier League football one day, and at this rate, there is no reason it can’t be with Stoke.

Robins has been in similar positions before, but to date, has not quite gotten over the line, at least not in the Championship, falling short with Coventry City and suffering a major dip in form last year with Stoke.

The 56-year-old will be well aware of the position he is in, what he has to do, and how to do it, but should still listen to the advice the former Bosnian international has laid out before him.

The January window presents Stoke with an opportunity to add one or two fresh bodies to the mix, and if they are to get over the line, those additions could be pivotal in their year, as transfer aims must be in place ahead of the coming months, whilst remaining consistent has to be the priority for now.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • However, Manchester United decided to contest the decision, and their appeal has now been successful.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have received a major boost ahead of their Premier League meeting with Brentford after the Football Association overturned Leny Yoro’s red card against Liverpool.

The defender was sent off just eight minutes into Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Anfield after bringing down Alexander Isak during a challenge that referee Sam Barrott judged to be a denial of a clear goalscoring opportunity.

However, Manchester United decided to contest the decision, and their appeal has now been successful. The FA confirmed that Yoro’s one-match suspension has been removed following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal.

According to recent reports, “The Manchester United player was sent off for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity during their Premier League match against Liverpool on Sunday 22 November. The independent Regulatory Commission’s written reasons for its decision will be published in due course,” the FA’s official statement read.

The decision means the French defender is available for Saturday’s meeting with Brentford at Old Trafford, giving Mauricio Pochettino another option in defence.

Mauricio Pochettino was furious with the original decision, particularly because it came so early in the game and left United playing with ten men for almost the entire match.

The United manager believed Isak’s heavy touch had taken the ball away from the Liverpool forward and put Senne Lammens in a position to collect it.

Speaking after the defeat, Pochettino questioned whether Yoro had actually committed a foul and insisted the defender had no intention of bringing Isak down.

“The ball wasn’t in his control,” Pochettino noted.

It has been revealed that “Isak, when he saw the control wasn’t good, it’s normal to delay, and stop to the run. In that moment that Yoro came from the back, and you go down.”.

The Argentine also made his feelings clear about the nature of the contact.

“But all that we play football; you know that wasn’t intentional. That is never a foul,” he added.

Industry observers note that the FA’s decision will come as a relief to Manchester United but perhaps too late. United suffered a heavy 4-0 defeat at Anfield after Yoro’s red. Pochettino would have had a chance in the game if VAR had overturned the red card, but United got another decision against them in the Premier League.

Although the appeal cannot change the outcome of the heavy defeat at Anfield, it at least means Pochettino will not lose one of his defensive options because of a decision that the club successfully challenged.
